title: Console: add reusable onboarding nudge component + targeting rules + dismissal persistence
author: Dylan Brooks
description: Summary: Implements a reusable, feature-flagged console nudge component used by the Lifecycle Growth Experiments sprint. Adds (1) a generic <NudgeCard/> UI with consistent layout, accessibility, and CTA patterns, (2) targeting rules for which nudge to show based on user activation state + page placement + experiment cohort, (3) dismissal persistence (server-backed with a local fallback) so users don’t see the same nudge repeatedly, and (4) basic analytics hooks for impressions/clicks/dismissals to support experiment readouts. Motivation: We need a lightweight in-console “next best action” system to reduce time-to-first-request and guide new users through API key creation → first request → enable streaming → view usage. This PR focuses on a minimal framework (not a full onboarding checklist). It’s designed to be iterated on via config + feature flags. Scope / notable behavior: - New NudgeCard component (title/body/CTA, optional secondary link, icon slot, compact vs default density). - Placements supported: dashboard header, api-keys empty state, quickstart panel. - Targeting model: given (userId, workspaceId, placement, currentRoute, activationState, cohortAssignment), pick a single nudge (highest priority) or none. - Dismissal persistence: Dismissals are stored as (user_id, nudge_id, nudge_version, placement) with a timestamp; server returns dismissed list for the user; client also caches to localStorage to avoid flicker before the server response arrives. Changing nudge_version will resurface the nudge (intended for copy/UX iterations). - Feature flags: gated behind lifecycle_growth_console_nudges_v1; cohort assignment read from existing experiment assignment service; includes explicit holdout behavior (do not render any nudges). - Analytics: emits product events for impression/click/dismiss; events include nudge_id, nudge_version, placement, route, cohort, and activation_state. No PII beyond internal IDs already present in standard console telemetry. Out of scope: complex multi-step checklist UI, personalization beyond activation state, or backend campaign management. Related: pairs with activation funnel eventing work (ENG-10492 / PR #28431) and the experiment flag rollouts (PR #28477).
commits: console/ui: add NudgeCard component + styles + a11y
console/nudges: add nudge registry + selection/prioritization logic
console/nudges: add dismissal persistence (API + local cache) + versioning
console/flags: gate nudge rendering behind lifecycle_growth_console_nudges_v1 + holdout
telemetry: add console_nudge_* analytics hooks (impression/click/dismiss) + tests
qa: add Playwright coverage for dismissal + holdout cohort behavior
testing: Unit: yarn test console-nudges + telemetry-events. E2E: Playwright spec covers (a) nudge renders for eligible cohort, (b) dismiss hides immediately and remains hidden after refresh, (c) holdout cohort renders nothing, (d) version bump causes resurface. Manual: verified on staging with test users in each activation state (no_api_key, has_key_no_request, has_request_no_streaming) and validated event emission in the debug telemetry panel.
rollout_plan: Keep feature flag OFF by default. Enable for internal dogfood first (25%) on staging, then 5% production for new signups only (signup_date >= 2026-01-20), then ramp to 50% if no UX regressions/support tickets. Holdout cohort (~10%) enforced at assignment layer. If issues: disable lifecycle_growth_console_nudges_v1 and/or force holdout for all cohorts; dismissal persistence is safe to leave in place (no user-visible surface without flag).

review_conversation: Marissa Cole: Can we ensure only ONE nudge shows at a time? I don’t want competing CTAs on dashboard. Also please confirm dismissal doesn’t block API key creation (we had issues with gating in the past). Dylan Brooks: Yep — selector returns a single nudge per placement; added a hard cap of 1 per page render and a priority table. Dismiss only hides the nudge card; it never disables underlying UI. Kenji Nakamura: Spacing/typography looks good but the “Dismiss” affordance is too subtle on mobile. Also CTA should be the only prominent button. Dylan Brooks: Updated to icon-button with tooltip and increased hitbox; secondary link now renders as text link (not a button) to avoid dual primaries. Nadia Rahman: Event names should align with the lifecycle taxonomy; please include nudge_version and placement and ensure impressions dedupe per page view. Dylan Brooks: Updated events to console_nudge_impression/click/dismiss and included required props. Added a per-render guard to avoid double-impression when React re-renders. Jada Williams: How does holdout work? We need deterministic assignment. Dylan Brooks: Uses the experiment assignment service (same as email). If cohort == holdout, selector returns null early and we do not emit impression events. Leila Farouk: Playwright test should cover refresh persistence and version bump. Dylan Brooks: Added both cases; also added a regression test for the api-keys empty state placement. Chloe Martin: Migration looks fine; please add an index on (user_id, placement). Dylan Brooks: Added composite index + updated query plan notes. Approvals: Marissa ✅, Kenji ✅, Nadia ✅, Jada ✅, Leila ✅, Chloe ✅.
release_notes: Console now supports a feature-flagged onboarding nudge card with targeting + dismissal persistence and telemetry hooks (internal use for Lifecycle Growth experiments).
